core_obligations: Use that M is I-power torsion to identify M tensor_R S with M, and note that flatness of R -> S gives a functorial base-change map Ext_R(M, N) -> Ext_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) (proof lines 24504-24515).
Observe that the statement of the lemma is precisely the surjectivity of this map and that the proof will establish it is an isomorphism (proof lines 24516-24518).

Use the presentation lemma to find a surjection M' -> M with M' a direct sum of modules of the form R/I^n, and use the six-term exact sequence together with the neighbourhood equivalence to reduce to M' (proof lines 24519-24524).
Further reduce, using compatibility of Ext with direct sums in a step the author states is omitted, to the single case M = R/I^n for some n (proof lines 24525-24526).

For M = R/I^n let f_1, ..., f_t generate I^n and use the explicit Ext description to obtain the displayed commutative diagram with exact rows relating Ext_R(R/I^n, N), H_1(N, f_bullet) and Hom_R(K, N) to their base-changed analogues, where K is the naive Koszul module; reduce to showing the two right vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 24529-24546).

Verify the two isomorphisms: Hom_R(K, N) = Hom_S(K tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) because K is annihilated by I^n, and H_1(N, f_bullet) tensor_R S = H_1(N tensor_R S, f_bullet) = H_1(N, f_bullet) using flatness of R -> S and that H_1(N, f_bullet) is annihilated by I^n (proof lines 24547-24555).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and says that for R-modules M and N with M being I-power torsion, every short exact sequence 0 -> N tensor_R S -> E-tilde -> M tensor_R S -> 0 descends to a commutative diagram of short exact sequences over R (source lines 24476-24501). The proof reformulates the statement as the assertion that the base-change map Ext_R(M, N) -> Ext_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism, and it proves the stronger isomorphism statement. The reduction is a genuine chain: since M is I-power torsion one has M tensor_R S = M; the base-change map on Ext is functorial because R -> S is flat (proof lines 24504-24515). Choosing by the presentation lemma a surjection M' -> M with M' a direct sum of modules R/I^n, the six-term exact sequence together with the neighbourhood equivalence reduces the claim to M' and then, using compatibility of Ext with direct sums in a step the author states is omitted, to the single case M = R/I^n (proof lines 24518-24526). The case M = R/I^n is done by writing f_1, ..., f_t for generators of I^n and using the explicit description of Ext in terms of Koszul homology: the proof displays a commutative diagram with exact rows relating Ext_R(R/I^n, N) to H_1(N, f_bullet) and Hom_R(K, N), where K is the module of the naive Koszul complex, and reduces to showing the two right-hand vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 24529-24546). That is then verified directly: Hom_R(K, N) = Hom_S(K tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) because K is annihilated by I^n, and H_1(N, f_bullet) tensor_R S = H_1(N tensor_R S, f_bullet) = H_1(N, f_bullet) because R -> S is flat and H_1(N, f_bullet) is annihilated by I^n (proof lines 24547-24555). The non-routine content is the reduction to M = R/I^n and the Koszul-homology comparison that finishes it.
